title: Cavity-vs-Loop Profile
description: Compares scalar-field transport along open cavities (single sightlines) versus closed loops (paired sightlines). The conformal clock shift is an exact differential and vanishes on any closed loop. The disformal transport is a squared derivative (always positive) and accumulates on a closed loop: both legs contribute positively. The loop isolates the disformal transport by canceling the conformal clock shift.

disformal.units: cm⁻¹ per B_eff (B_eff in cm); c × B_eff × I_dis in cm/s
disformal.loop: accumulates (sum of both legs, always positive)
disformal.static_field_note: For ∂₀φ = 0, disformal term B(φ)(∂₀φ)² = 0 in g̃₀₀; disformal affects spatial metric only, not clock rates.

key_result.assessment: The conformal clock shift is a cavity-only signal that vanishes on any closed loop (exact differential). The disformal transport integral accumulates on a closed loop — both legs contribute positively because (∂_ℓ φ)² is always positive regardless of traversal direction. The loop isolates the disformal transport by canceling the conformal part. For a static field, the disformal sector does not affect clock rates (g̃₀₀); it affects photon propagation through the spatial metric. The two observables are physically distinct: conformal is a spectroscopic velocity shift, disformal is an optical time-transfer phase delay. Gate 4B-0: the edge-core differential does not survive loop closure in the conformal sector; the disformal transport is the only nonzero loop residue, and it accumulates (sum), not partially cancels (difference).
